purpose: Review what persistent object prototypes should store for concept recognition, dense instance grouping, and occlusion-aware visible segmentation.

sources.title: This Looks Like That: Deep Learning for Interpretable Image Recognition
sources.read_scope: Original paper architecture and training sections; prototype grounding/projection also checked against the indexed original text.
sources.supports: Class-discriminative prototypical local evidence grounded in latent training patches.
sources.boundary: Classification evidence does not establish dense instance separation or pig segmentation gains.

sources.title: Deformable ProtoPNet: An Interpretable Image Classifier Using Deformable Prototypes
sources.read_scope: Original abstract, Sections 3.1-3.2 method excerpts and prototype reasoning passages.
sources.supports: Prototypes composed of parts with input-dependent relative spatial deformation.
sources.boundary: Pose-tolerant classification is not proof of instance ownership.

sources.title: ShapeMask: Learning to Segment Novel Objects by Refining Shape Priors
sources.read_scope: Original Sections 3.1 and 3.3, abstract and method overview; CVF indexed method text checked as corroboration.
sources.supports: Shape priors from normalized training-mask clusters plus instance-conditioned refinement.
sources.boundary: Legitimate evidence for mask-derived priors; does not establish current SPM memory or cross-instance ownership.

sources.title: Compositional Convolutional Neural Networks: A Deep Architecture with Innate Robustness to Partial Occlusion
sources.read_scope: Original Section 3.1 and indexed Section 4 evaluation/occluder-localization passages.
sources.supports: Local feature distributions, spatial compositions and competing object/occluder explanations.
sources.boundary: Main empirical tasks are occluded classification and occluder localization, not normal YOLO mask AP.

sources.title: Amodal Segmentation through Out-of-Task and Out-of-Distribution Generalization with a Bayesian Model
sources.read_scope: Original Sections 3.2-3.3 and evaluation conditions in Section 4, including known versus unknown center conditions.
sources.supports: Explicit foreground, context, pose-conditioned shape and occlusion variables in a neural-feature generative model.
sources.boundary: Proposal and center privileges must remain distinct from deployed normal-output metrics.

sources.title: Object-Centric Learning with Slot Attention
sources.read_scope: Original abstract and Section 2.1, including slot-axis normalization and iterative update equations.
sources.supports: Competitive binding of current input features into exchangeable runtime entity representations.
sources.boundary: Runtime slots are not persistent category prototypes; slot budget is not a certified instance count.

sources.title: Bridging the Gap to Real-World Object-Centric Learning
sources.read_scope: Original Sections 3.1-3.2 and the discussion of image reconstruction versus pretrained feature targets.
sources.supports: Pretrained feature reconstruction with competitive grouping can yield object-centric representations on real images.
sources.boundary: Counters a blanket rejection of feature reconstruction; does not validate current SPM or imply anatomical correspondence.

sources.title: InstanceCut: from Edges to Instances with MultiCut
sources.read_scope: Original abstract and Section 3.1 framework overview; indexed original graph-partition formulation also inspected.
sources.supports: Combining semantic evidence with instance-aware boundaries for instance partitioning.
sources.boundary: Graph boundary grouping alone does not supply a complete model of disconnected occluded parts.

sources.title: Instance Segmentation by Jointly Optimizing Spatial Embeddings and Clustering Bandwidth
sources.read_scope: Original abstract, Section 3 overview and Section 3.1, with indexed original explanation of instance-specific margins and seeds.
sources.supports: Instance-specific pixel association using spatial embeddings and adaptive clustering ranges.
sources.boundary: Per-image instance embeddings and centers are transient state, not a persistent object knowledge library.

sources.title: Pixel-Grounded Prototypical Part Networks
sources.read_scope: Original Sections 3-4 excerpts on receptive fields, visualization and corrected pixel-space mappings.
sources.supports: Prototype interpretations require faithful spatial grounding rather than appealing heatmaps alone.
sources.boundary: Part visualizability does not by itself prove segmentation utility or a unique semantic factor.

sources.title: Coding of Border Ownership in Monkey Visual Cortex
sources.read_scope: Primary-paper database abstract and indexed original full-text excerpts on contextual integration and border ownership; direct PMC open presented an access challenge.
sources.supports: Macaque visual neurons can encode border ownership using broader figure-ground context.
sources.boundary: Does not establish a serial human apple-recognition pipeline or identify an optimal artificial architecture.

sources.title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts
sources.read_scope: Original Section 3 presence-token explanation and Appendices A.1, C.2 and F.4 counting details.
sources.supports: Separation of concept presence and per-instance localization; concepts can be reused to identify multiple instances.
sources.boundary: Not a direct prototype-bank experiment; the report states the presence token does not help its counting setup and handles group-versus-individual duplicates separately.

sources.title: Dynamic Routing Between Capsules
sources.read_scope: Original abstract and introduction excerpts explaining entity states, part-to-whole predictions, and iterative routing by agreement.
sources.supports: Parts predict whole-entity states; mutually consistent predictions support an entity and guide dynamic assignment.
sources.boundary: Overlapping digit recognition does not establish real pig instance segmentation or a complete top-down feedback system.

sources.title: Matrix Capsules with EM Routing
sources.read_scope: Original abstract and introduction excerpts on learned part-whole transformations, pose votes and EM assignments.
sources.supports: Learned transformations encode part-whole relationships while input-specific assignment coefficients group compatible pose votes.
sources.boundary: smallNORB classification results do not establish the optimal routing or segmentation gains for the present task.

inferences_by_this_review: Prefer evidence-grounded local parts and appearance together with deformable spatial composition and conditional ownership/occlusion priors for the stated SPM goal.
Keep persistent reusable knowledge distinct from current per-instance pose, location, visibility, ownership and count.
Use the brain analogy as a functional design motivation rather than a biological equivalence claim.
No cited paper establishes that this synthesis is optimal or effective on the current pig segmentation task.
user_clarification: Jointly learn part prototypes, whole-object prototypes and their compositional relationships, with mutual constraints between local evidence and whole-instance hypotheses.
